newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall from highs, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall from highs, seen rebounding.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday eased from a 34-month high but analysts said the strong buying after price fixing suggested the market would soon return to the two-month 32-percent bull run seen spurred by foreign buying.

"The market still looks strong -- the correction after such growth was small, and there will likely be growth tomorrow, signalled by gains today by large-cap stocks," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Large-cap banks BPH and BRE rose 1.8 and 2.9 percent respectively in impressive 20.6-million ($6.8 million) and 10.9-million-zloty ($3.6 million) turnovers.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 17,543.7 points and turnover fell 16.5 percent to 242.2 million zlotys ($80.4) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 60 to 14 with 14 stocks flat.

Analysts said two other banks, Bank Gdanski and BIG, jumped 5.7 percent and 4.3 percent respectively after a newspaper report that BIG's plan to up its 31.2-percent stake in Gdanski by 31.9-percent would happen on February 21.

Some analysts said a deeper correction for the overall market was soon possible. "The rises seem to be losing their rationality..., they are not justified by company earnings," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Bank Pekao brokerage.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 2.9 percent to 165 zlotys ($54.8) in 71.5-million-zloty ($23.7 million) trade and were flat at 163 zlotys ($54.1) in 23.6-million-zloty ($7.8 million) continuous trade.
Live trade turnover was at 24.8 million zlotys ($8.2 million) with nine stocks up, six down and six flat and the WIG 20 index gaining 1.6 percent to 1,832 points.
